question.text: SEBI has outlined a Code of Conduct for members of the Investment Committee which includes. Which of the following is NOT a specified duty of IC members?

answer.text: Maintaining integrity and the highest ethical and professional standards of conduct
Disclosing conflicts and recusing from decision making where necessary
Maintaining confidentiality of AIF, investor and investee company information
Personally indemnifying the AIF for any investment losses on approved deals

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.10 (Code of Conduct), IC members must: (i) maintain integrity and highest ethical/professional standards, (ii) disclose conflicts in a timely manner and recuse where necessary, (iii) maintain confidentiality, and (iv) not indulge in unethical/fraud acts. Personal indemnification for investment losses is NOT a duty — IC members have fiduciary duty, not guarantor status. **The Trap:** Options A, B, C are explicit Code items. Option D is a common misconception — IC members approve based on due care, not personally guarantee outcomes. Losses on diligently approved deals do not trigger personal liability absent fraud/gross negligence. **Cross-Exam Context:** Same carve-out appears in Companies Act 2013 Section 166 for directors: duty of care, not outcome-guarantee. Tested in XV and III-A. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Offer your external IC members D&O insurance (Directors & Officers cover) — without it, quality external members decline appointments. Premium is usually fund-borne expense disclosed in PPM.
